title: Stochastic convex-concave saddle-point problems: expected global gap

description_paragraphs: Solve $\min_{x\in X}\max_{y\in Y}f(x,y)$.

assumptions.scope: All point pairs in the declared function domain. Blockwise constants are uniform in the remaining fixed variables.
assumptions.description: For every fixed $y$, the function $f(\cdot,y)$ is convex. For every fixed $x$, the function $f(x,\cdot)$ is concave.

assumptions.description: The population joint gradient satisfies $\|\nabla f(z)-\nabla f(w)\|\le\beta\|z-w\|$. Same-sample mean-square smoothness of stochastic gradients is not required.
The feasible domain is nonempty, compact, and convex, with $\operatorname{diam}(K)\le D_K$; for saddle problems, $K=X\times Y$.

model.parameter_domain_description: $D_K$: positive real; $\beta$: positive real; $d$: integer at least 2; $\varepsilon$: positive real; $\sigma$: positive real. Derived quantities are defined in the parameter table. Each region states any additional accuracy and dimension conditions.
description_paragraphs: The set $K\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ is known, nonempty, compact, and convex, with $\operatorname{diam}(K)\le D_K$. The conditions $K=X\times Y$ and $d=d_x+d_y$ also hold.
The function $f$ is convex in $x$, concave in $y$, and has a jointly $\beta$-Lipschitz gradient.
These assumptions ensure the relevant solutions exist; all vector norms are Euclidean.

description_paragraphs: Public inputs include block dimensions $d_x,d_y$ and $D_K$, $\beta$, $\varepsilon$, and $\sigma$, together with the stated initial-point and feasible-domain information. Analytic representations of hidden functions, operators, or matrices are not revealed.

$$
z\in K\longmapsto G_f(z;\xi)=(G_x,G_y)
$$
Exact Euclidean projection onto the known set is allowed. Its calls are recorded separately and excluded from the primary query count.

Let $\mathcal H_t$ denote the full history before query t. Conditional on $\mathcal H_t,z_t$, the response $G_t\in\mathbb R^{d_x+d_y}$ satisfies $\mathbb E[G_t\mid\mathcal H_t,z_t]=\nabla f(z_t)$ and $\mathbb E[\|G_t-\nabla f(z_t)\|_2^2\mid\mathcal H_t,z_t]\le\sigma^2$. Each call uses an independent fresh sample.

No reusable sample identifier or cross-point sample reuse is available. No mean-square smoothness of sample gradients or operators is additionally assumed. Blocks within a full vector may be correlated.

bounds.derivation: Use the primal interval $[-D_K/2,D_K/2]$, a singleton dual domain, and linear payoffs $f_\pm(x,y)=\pm ax$ with $a=8\varepsilon/D_K$. Fresh primal-gradient samples are Gaussian with mean $\pm a$ and variance $\sigma^2$. A wrong-half-axis output has saddle gap at least $4\varepsilon$, so the expected-gap guarantee implies a sign test with error at most $1/4$. The per-sample KL divergence $2a^2/\sigma^2$ yields the query lower bound $\Omega(\sigma^2D_K^2/\varepsilon^2)$.
bounds.lower_scope_type_note: Two-point testing, zero-query indistinguishability, and nonexistence counterexamples cover arbitrary privately randomized policies. These are not linear-span lower bounds.
